daily.title: Binance crypto exchange suspends trades over North Korea-linked hack
daily.summary: Crypto platform Binance has suspended trading following a suspected hack now linked to North Korea. The disruption has left users unable to trade on the cryptocurrency platform while the suspected breach is investigated.

daily.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
daily.summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

daily.title: Russia: Critical newspaper 'Novaya Gazeta' to close
daily.summary: "Novaya Gazeta," one of the last remaining independent, critical media outlets in Russia, has announced it is closing under pressure from state authorities. Meanwhile, in Ukraine, evacuations have begun in Oleshky.

daily.title: Brazil's new anti-gang law: Can it curb organized crime?
daily.summary: A tough stance against organized crime? One year after a massacre that left more than 130 people dead, a new law aims to crack down on drug cartels in Rio's favelas.

daily.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
daily.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

daily.title: Many Turkish 'guest workers' hit by poverty in old age
daily.summary: West Germany and Turkey signed an agreement allowing the temporary recruitment of workers on October 30, 1961. Sixty-five years on, many so-called 'guest workers' can't live from their pensions.

daily.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
daily.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

daily.title: Germany news: Merz in Asia warns against weaponizing trade
daily.summary: German diplomacy in Asia takes focus this week, as Chancellor Merz wraps up a three-country Asian business tour in South Korea. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier held talks with Xi Jinping in Beijing. DW has more.

daily.title: India news: Space agency to boost GPS alternative with new satellite
daily.summary: The Indian national space agency's mission aims to strengthen its indigenous navigation system and reduce reliance on the US-owned GPS. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi renewed his call for more election protests. DW has more.

daily.title: Israeli election: Netanyahu, main rival fall short of majority after all votes counted
daily.summary: With all the votes counted, the pro-Netanyahu bloc finished ahead of Gadi Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc. But tough coalition talks loom as neither grouping won a majority. DW has more.

daily.title: Venezuela: Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado says US backs 2027 election
daily.summary: The return of Maria Corina Machado, who says Trump opened the "floodgate to freedom" for Venezuela, presents a challenge for Washington as Trump has also backed interim President Delcy Rodriguez.

daily.title: Bayer wins Roundup cancer trial after Supreme Court ruling
daily.summary: The weedkiller Roundup has been accused of being carcinogenic to humans despite no warning on its label. Bayer is seeking to settle tens of thousands of further cases.

daily.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
daily.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

daily.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
daily.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

daily.title: Justice for Maya women in Guatemala, girls back in school in India, restored land in Mali: The UN has named its 2026 SDG Action Award winners
daily.summary: Champions of indigenous women's rights in Guatemala, girls' education in India, and restored farmland in Mali all featured among the winners of UN's SDG Action Awards.

daily.title: Berlin's Elif Eralp under fire over Der Spiegel interview
daily.summary: Left candidate Elif Eralp has sparked controversy after Der Spiegel reported she was advised against mentioning a pro-Palestinian activist for fear of reprisals against her family.

daily.title: Iraq: Life sentences for 3 French 'Islamic State' suspects
daily.summary: The three were among 47 French "Islamic State" suspects transferred from Syrian detention. So far, ten French nationals have received prison terms after being convicted of belonging to the group.

daily.title: EU seeks 'highest level' ties with Canada in Montreal summit
daily.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said EU seeks "association without accession" for Canada, after EU members snub "associate member" designation.

daily.title: Israel election: Authorities dispute Netanyahu's fraud claims
daily.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud claims large-scale foreign involvement in the elections led by Qatar and Turkey, with Israel’s authorities so far refuting the claims.

daily.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
daily.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

daily.title: Germany seeks new head of state
daily.summary: The question of who should become Germany's new presiden is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

daily.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
daily.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

weekly.title: US moves to lift sanctions on Russia's shadow fleet could undermine Western pressure on Moscow and help fund its war in Ukraine.
weekly.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

weekly.title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
weekly.summary: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

weekly.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
weekly.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

weekly.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
weekly.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

weekly.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
weekly.summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

weekly.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
weekly.summary: Young people in Germany are preparing to protest over education and climate change. Politicians fear violence like in France, but an expert sees differences.

weekly.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
weekly.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

weekly.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
weekly.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

weekly.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
weekly.summary: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

weekly.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
weekly.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

weekly.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
weekly.summary: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

weekly.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
weekly.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

weekly.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
weekly.summary: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

weekly.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
weekly.summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

weekly.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
weekly.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

weekly.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
weekly.summary: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

weekly.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
weekly.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But ahead of the US midterm elections, does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

weekly.title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
weekly.summary: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

weekly.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
weekly.summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

weekly.title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
weekly.summary: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

weekly.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
weekly.summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

weekly.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
weekly.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

weekly.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
weekly.summary: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

weekly.title: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
weekly.summary: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

developing.title: Live: Fresh protests hit France amid heightened security
developing.summary: Police and elite security forces are out in force in French cities as thousands participate in a new round of protests. The protest location was changed last minute in Paris. Follow DW.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
